newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Industry group finalises proposals on information society.
newsitem.headline: Industry group finalises proposals on information society.

text.p: A high-level industry advisory group is expected to urge the European Union to promote the "information society" by taking action in areas including telecommunications, electronic commerce and standardisation.
The group, set up by Industry Commissioner Martin Bangemann, has not yet finalised its proposals.
But at a meeting last week in Berlin, it debated a discussion paper on questions ranging from how to bring the Internet into schools to how to regulate disputes over telecoms liberalisation.

It also discussed proposals on issues including satellites, public administrations, research and "technological convergence" between the telecoms, computer and media industries, European Commission and industry officials said.
The group, which includes about 30 company executives, is looking at ways to ensure that the EU takes full advantage of the revolution in telecoms, media and computer technology.
The discussion paper, which was made available to reporters, proposes setting up a committee of national telecoms regulators and possibly drawing up a European Telecommunications Act.

It also suggests that the EU set a target date for wiring up all schools, colleges, universities and libraries to the Internet, set up a framework for information security through digital signatures and encryption and promote use of the new technologies by national governments.
It says the Commission should examine the need for new regulatory initiatives to address the convergence question.

Carlo De Benedetti, honorary chairman of Italian computer company Olivetti, told the group the EU should set 1999 as a deadline for removing the EU's remaining internal trade barriers, to coincide with the advent of the single currency, an Olivetti spokesman told Reuters.
De Benedetti heads a working group on regulatory issues.

"Mr De Benedetti underlined the need to link closely the building up of the information society with the actual completion of the internal market, particulary in the services area," the spokesman said.

The group agreed to meet again to finalise its report, Commission spokesman Jochen Kubosch. It also agreed that Bangemann and Etienne Davignon, president of Belgian holding company Societe Generale de Belgique, should discuss the proposals with the Dutch presidency.

Davignon heads a working group on competitiveness, employment, education and training. Thomas Middlehoff, a member of the board of German media group Bertelsmann AG, heads a third working group on standardisation and electronic commerce.
